value.body: Studies rocks, minerals, soil and groundwater to locate resources such as ores, coal, oil and water, and to judge ground conditions for construction. Mining and exploration companies, oil and gas firms, consultancies and government departments hire geologists. Work splits between fieldwork (mapping, sampling, logging drill cores) and office work on maps, data and reports.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: M.Sc / M.Sc Tech in Geology or Applied Geology
items.note: B.Sc graduates usually start as field or geology assistants

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Geological maps, Brunton compass, GPS, GIS software, microscopes

items.label: Government route
items.note: For Geological Survey of India and groundwater posts; needs a master's

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Most geologist posts expect a master's in Geology or Applied Geology. With a B.Sc, entry is usually as a field or exploration assistant with an exploration, mining or consultancy firm. After an M.Sc, routes include company hiring, GATE (Geology & Geophysics) for some PSUs, and the UPSC Combined Geo-Scientist Examination for central posts.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Reading and making geological maps (including GIS)

value.title: At a glance
items: Long field stints in remote areas are common, especially early on.
A master's is the usual entry level for geologist titles.
Specialisations include exploration, mining, hydrogeology, engineering geology and petroleum geology.
